stages.name: Independent or neutral
stages.desc: Free of Sparta, Athens and Persia, or siding with none

stages.name: Spartan-controlled
stages.desc: Ruled by Sparta's governors (harmosts) or its client oligarchies

stages.name: Athenian or allied
stages.desc: Athens and the cities and kings fighting with it against Sparta

stages.name: Persian
stages.desc: Ruled by the Great King's satraps or tributary rulers

stages.name: Phoenician & Cypriot fleet bases
stages.desc: Shipyards and crews of the King's fleet under Conon

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Kition, Amathus, Paphos and Soli: island kingdoms paying tribute to Persia
The Cypriot kingdoms fit out triremes for the King's fleet
Evagoras extends his rule over most of Cyprus and defies Persia
The King's Peace assigns Cyprus to Persia; Evagoras fights on alone

states.name: Israel
timeline: Coastal towns under Sidon and Tyre; the hills part of the satrapy Beyond the River

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Part of the Persian satrapy Beyond the River

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Sidon, Tyre and Byblos: Phoenician city-kingdoms under Persian rule
Phoenician shipyards fit out triremes for the King's new fleet
The Phoenician fleet now turns against Evagoras of Cyprus

states.name: Syria
timeline: The Persian satrapy 'Beyond the River', with the Phoenician island city of Arwad
Cyrus the Younger marches through on his way to Babylon

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Satrapies of Tissaphernes at Sardis and Pharnabazus at Dascylium; Lysander's fleet bases at Ephesus
Sparta sends Thibron to defend the Ionian cities: war on the Aegean coast
King Agesilaus campaigns in Lydia and Phrygia
After Cnidus, the coastal cities expel their Spartan garrisons and welcome Conon
The King's Peace hands the Greek cities of Asia to Persia

states.name: Greece
timeline: Lysander's fleet rules the Aegean after Aegospotami; Athens is under siege
Athens surrenders; Spartan governors and boards of ten rule the islands
Thebes, Athens, Corinth and Argos ally against Sparta: the Corinthian War begins
After Cnidus the islands expel their Spartan governors; the allies hold the Isthmus
Conon's crews and Persian money rebuild the Long Walls of Athens
The King's Peace leaves Sparta the enforcer of Greek 'autonomy'

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Desert and caravan country of the Persian satrapy Beyond the River

states.name: Egypt
timeline: A Persian satrapy, already shaken by revolt in the Delta
Amyrtaeus of Sais throws off Persian rule: Egypt is independent
Pharaoh Nepherites sends grain and ship gear to Sparta
Pharaoh Achoris allies with Evagoras and Athens against Persia
The King's Peace leaves Egypt to face Persia without Athens

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: Evagoras rules Salamis as a Persian vassal and shelters the fugitive Conon
The shipyards of Salamis build triremes for Conon's fleet
Evagoras breaks with Persia, backed by Athens and later Egypt
Abandoned by Athens under the King's Peace, Evagoras fights Persia alone

states.name: Cyprus U.N. Buffer Zone
timeline: The plain of Cyprus between Salamis and the southern kingdoms
Timber and crews for Conon's fleet
Under Evagoras, at war with Persia
Evagoras fights on alone after the King's Peace

events.title: Aegospotami
events.text: Lysander surprises the Athenian fleet beached on the Hellespont and takes some 170 ships; Conon escapes with eight.

events.title: Refuge in Cyprus
events.text: Conon sails to Salamis in Cyprus, where King Evagoras, a friend of Athens, takes him in.

events.title: Athens surrenders
events.text: Starved by blockade, Athens gives up its fleet; the Long Walls are pulled down to the music of flute girls.

events.title: The Thirty
events.text: A Spartan-backed junta of thirty oligarchs rules Athens and kills some fifteen hundred citizens.

events.title: Samos falls
events.text: The last loyal ally of Athens surrenders to Lysander; his boards of ten rule the Aegean cities.

events.title: Egypt breaks free
events.text: Amyrtaeus of Sais throws off Persian rule in the Nile Delta.

events.title: Democracy restored
events.text: Democrats under Thrasybulus win at Piraeus; the Thirty fall and Sparta allows democracy back.

events.title: Cyrus marches
events.text: Prince Cyrus leaves Sardis with ten thousand Greek mercenaries, and quiet Spartan help, to seize his brother's throne.

events.title: The Ten Thousand
events.text: After Cyrus dies at Cunaxa, his Greek mercenaries fight their way north and reach the sea at Trapezus.

events.title: Sparta fights Persia
events.text: Sparta sends Thibron to protect the Ionian cities from the satrap Tissaphernes.

events.title: Dercylidas in the Troad
events.text: The Spartan general takes nine Aeolian towns from Pharnabazus in eight days.

events.title: Nepherites I
events.text: A new pharaoh at Mendes founds Egypt's Twenty-ninth Dynasty and courts Sparta.

events.title: Conon's commission
events.text: Pharnabazus wins the King's approval: Conon is given 500 talents to build a fleet in Cyprus.

events.title: Phoenician shipyards
events.text: Sidon, Tyre and the other Phoenician cities fit out triremes for the King's fleet.

events.title: Siege of Caunus
events.text: Conon's forty ships are blockaded in Caunus by 120 Spartan triremes until Persian troops relieve him.

events.title: Rhodes revolts
events.text: The Rhodians expel the Spartan fleet and open their harbour to Conon.

events.title: Grain for Sparta seized
events.text: Conon captures a convoy of Egyptian grain and ship gear sent by Nepherites to Sparta.

events.title: Agesilaus at Aulis
events.text: Sparta's king sacrifices at Aulis like Agamemnon before crossing to Asia; Boeotian horsemen break up the rite.

events.title: Victory at Sardis
events.text: Agesilaus beats the Persian cavalry by the Pactolus; the King has Tissaphernes beheaded.

events.title: Persian gold
events.text: Timocrates of Rhodes brings 50 talents to Thebes, Corinth and Argos to start a war against Sparta.

events.title: Lysander killed
events.text: The victor of Aegospotami falls under the walls of Haliartus in Boeotia.

events.title: Mutiny at Caunus
events.text: Unpaid Cypriot rowers mutiny; Conon travels to the King himself to demand money for his men.

events.title: Battle of Nemea
events.text: Sparta wins the largest hoplite battle of the war near Corinth.

events.title: Battle of Cnidus
events.text: In August Conon and Pharnabazus destroy Sparta's fleet; the admiral Peisander dies, and fifty triremes are taken.

events.title: Battle of Coronea
events.text: Agesilaus, recalled from Asia, tells his men Sparta won at sea, and fights through the allied line.

events.title: The islands freed
events.text: Cos, Nisyros, Teos, Chios and Mytilene expel their Spartan governors.

events.title: Ephesus opens its gates
events.text: The Ionian cities welcome Conon, promised freedom from Spartan garrisons.

events.title: Abydos holds
events.text: Dercylidas keeps Abydos and Sestos on the Hellespont loyal to Sparta.

events.title: Raid on Laconia
events.text: The fleet ravages Sparta's coast and seizes Cythera, garrisoned by an Athenian governor.

events.title: Silver for Corinth
events.text: At the Isthmus, Pharnabazus gives the allied council money to keep fighting Sparta.

events.title: Conon in Piraeus
events.text: Conon sails in with eighty ships; his rowers and Persian money finish the Long Walls.

events.title: Statue for Conon
events.text: Athens sets up bronze statues of Conon and Evagoras in the Agora.

events.title: Conon arrested
events.text: At Sardis the satrap Tiribazus jails Conon while hearing Sparta's envoy Antalcidas.

events.title: Evagoras defies Persia
events.text: Amathus, Soli and Kition appeal to the King as Evagoras extends his rule over Cyprus.

events.title: Lechaeum
events.text: Athenian light troops under Iphicrates destroy a Spartan regiment near Corinth.

events.title: Ships for Cyprus lost
events.text: A Spartan squadron captures ten Athenian triremes sailing to help Evagoras.

events.title: Byzantium tolls
events.text: Thrasybulus revives Athenian tolls on Black Sea shipping at the Bosporus.

events.title: Achoris joins
events.text: Egypt's pharaoh Achoris allies with Evagoras and Athens.

events.title: Thrasybulus killed
events.text: The hero of Athenian democracy dies at Aspendus, raising money for his fleet.

events.title: Hellespont closed
events.text: Antalcidas, with Persian and Syracusan ships, blocks Athens' grain route.

events.title: The King's Peace
events.text: Tiribazus reads Artaxerxes' decree: the cities of Asia and Cyprus belong to the King.

events.title: Sworn at Sparta
events.text: The Greek states swear to the Peace; Sparta becomes its enforcer.

chartNote: Share of the area of the present-day countries on the map, by the power that dominated each. Regions are today's boundaries and a simplification: Greece held both Athens and Sparta, Turkey's Aegean coast changed hands while its interior stayed Persian, and Cyprus was several kingdoms. Dates follow Xenophon and Diodorus, who often disagree.
